title: Samsung Electro-Mechanics Signs $210M AI Server MLCC and Inductor Supply Deal
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · September 29, 2026

Samsung Electro-Mechanics (KRX: 009150) signed a KRW 285 billion (about US$210 million) long-term supply agreement to provide MLCCs and inductors for AI servers to an unnamed global big-tech company. Here is what the contract covers, why MLCCs and inductors matter more as AI servers get more powerful, and what was not disclosed.

CompanyRoleEvidence
Samsung Electro-Mechanics
KRX: 009150		Supplier of MLCCs and inductors for AI servers under a new one-year long-term agreementFiling (LTA disclosure, Sep 29, 2026)

What was disclosed

  • Contract value: KRW 285 billion, about US$210 million.
  • Term: one year, from January 1 to December 31 next year.
  • Scale: equal to 2.5% of Samsung Electro-Mechanics' consolidated revenue last year.
  • Products: MLCCs (multilayer ceramic capacitors) and inductors for AI servers.
  • Customer: disclosed only as an unnamed "global big-tech company," which the company said is confidential for business reasons. We do not name a customer here because none was disclosed.
  • Context: this is the fifth long-term supply agreement (LTA) Samsung Electro-Mechanics has disclosed this year.

Why MLCCs and inductors matter more as AI servers scale up

MLCCs regulate current flow in electronic circuits and block signal interference between components; inductors stabilize power supply against current fluctuations and reduce noise generated during power conversion. As AI servers and data centers pack in more compute, their power draw and power fluctuation both increase, which raises the bar for both parts: MLCCs need higher capacitance and reliability, and inductors need to handle higher current more efficiently while staying reliable. Samsung Electro-Mechanics said it is advancing high-capacitance, high-reliability MLCC technology and expanding development of high-current, high-efficiency, high-reliability inductors specifically to match AI servers' power characteristics.

Reading the repeat-LTA pattern

This is Samsung Electro-Mechanics' fifth disclosed long-term supply agreement this year, which suggests a pattern of locking in AI-related component demand through fixed-term contracts rather than one-off orders, similar to the customer-backed FC-BGA capex the company announced the same week (see our Samsung Electro-Mechanics FC-BGA brief). A Samsung Electro-Mechanics representative said that as the global AI market's technology advances, the performance and reliability bar required of MLCCs is also rising, and that the company is expanding cooperation with global customers on the strength of differentiated technology and stable supply capacity.

What is not disclosed

  • The customer's name or industry (server maker, hyperscaler, or component integrator are all possible).
  • Unit volumes or specific product model numbers covered by the agreement.
  • Whether this agreement is a renewal or expansion of a prior relationship with the same customer.

Quick FAQ

How large is this Samsung Electro-Mechanics contract?
KRW 285 billion (about $210 million), running for one year starting January 1 next year, equal to 2.5% of the company's 2025 consolidated revenue.

What is being supplied?
MLCCs (multilayer ceramic capacitors) and inductors, both used to stabilize power delivery in AI servers.

Who is the customer?
Not disclosed. Samsung Electro-Mechanics named it only as a "global big-tech company," citing confidentiality.

Is this related to Samsung Electro-Mechanics' FC-BGA investment news?
Not stated as connected, but both this LTA and the FC-BGA capex plan point to the same underlying driver: rising AI server demand for advanced components.
